we provide a theoretical framework for transfer learning in reinforcement learning that enables an agent, starting from a set of base skills, to learn a new task in a fast and sample-efficient manner.

we present a framework for lifelong reinforcement learning that allows for generalisation over an unknown task distribution by leveraging logical composition, we show how to use logical composition in the context of transfer learning in reinforcement learning, we provide a theoretical bound on the performance of transferred policies, and we provide theoretical results on the number of tasks that are necessary and sufficient to generalise over an unknown task space

logical composition can be used in reinforcement learning to (1) learn a policy for a new task by transferring a previously learned policy, and (2) enable the agent to generalise over the distribution of tasks.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we propose a novel framework for lifelong reinforcement learning that is able to generalise over an unknown distribution of tasks, while learning only a few of them.
we provide a theoretical foundation for transfer learning in reinforcement learning and show that it can be applied in the lifelong setting, where an agent receives new tasks throughout its lifetime.
we propose a framework that allows an agent to learn a set of tasks in an online fashion, and then generalise to new tasks by transferring knowledge from previous tasks.
The main takeaway from our work is that
logical composition is a powerful tool for generalisation and transfer in lifelong reinforcement learning.
we can use logical composition to generalise over an arbitrary distribution of tasks, even when the agent is only given a few tasks to learn from.
logical composition enables agents to generalise over an unknown task distribution by learning an interpretable representation of its knowledge.
